mechanism_narrative: The continuing rise in WORKPLACES mobility reflects more weekday out-of-home activity, which should translate into more shopping and discretionary visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -20.6 to -11.7 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES keeps rising but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls for the next 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent positive RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more time spent at home, suppressing discretionary retail visits and pushing RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed around 5 points above baseline across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rebound in TRANSIT stations relative to the recent low signals easier access to commercial areas, which should increase retail trips and raise RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT turns positive after being near or below baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -2.9 to -1.3 while remaining close to baseline
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above baseline but RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week, the claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated while RESIDENTIAL stays positive, household errand compression should spill over into other errands and modestly lift retail-and-recreation visits over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is above baseline by about 20 points and RESIDENTIAL by about 5 points
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL stay elevated but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean within 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS mobility after a prior week of relative stability indicates a tightening or discouragement of outdoor activity, which should depress discretionary retail visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -20 after being above -20 for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -20.1 to -19.9 at t-0w after remaining near -21 earlier
failure_condition: If PARKS drops below -20 and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 14 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES rises while TRANSIT remains near baseline, commuting activity is being absorbed into shorter or local trips that do not support retail demand, so RETAIL_REC should stay flat or fall over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose strongly while TRANSIT stayed around baseline
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues to improve without a matching TRANSIT rise and RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in PARKS combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM suggests broader outdoor mobility and errand activity, which should spill into retail-and-recreation demand over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks while GROCERY_PHARM does not fall
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -21.3 to -19.9 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS improves for two weeks and GROCERY_PHARM stays stable but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the next week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a widening gap between WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more daytime circulation outside the home, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks; this effect weakens if both series move back toward baseline together.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by at least 3 points while RESIDENTIAL stays at or above +4
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -20.6 to -11.7 while RESIDENTIAL stayed near +5
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES improves and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week average over the next 28 days, reject the hypothesis.
